extracted.intended_audience: early-career scientists and prospective applicants to Damon Runyon award programs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/selection criteria for applying to Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation award programs, aimed at identifying and supporting early-career scientists pursuing innovative cancer-related research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission / funding focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Damon Runyon’s mission is to identify and support the best early career scientists pursuing innovative research that has the potential to transform cancer prevention, diagnosis and treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goal: encourage new generations of outstanding researchers to pursue paradigm-shifting ideas and approaches and have highly productive, successful research careers. Emphasis on transformative potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of research funded (breadth)
rubrics_metrics.description: Damon Runyon views cancer research very broadly, including the full spectrum of basic questions important to normal human biology and carcinogenesis, as well as development of new platforms and technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages all theoretical and experimental research that has the potential to provide insights into cancer and the search for cancer causes, mechanisms, therapies and prevention for all types of cancer. Explicit examples: molecular biology, genetics, genomics, cell biology, immunology, model organisms, microbiology, virology, systems biology, structural biology, neuroscience, aging, chemistry, chemical biology, organic synthesis, physics and quantitative biology – in addition to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty and risk tolerance
rubrics_metrics.description: We seek novel ideas and approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foundation understands many ideas/experiments do not work and is willing to take risks on creative new ideas and approaches, even if they may 'fail.' Applicants are encouraged to propose novel, potentially high-reward work. (See 'our current projects' for examples.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant quality — productivity, creativity, and problem selection
rubrics_metrics.description: We seek individuals who have demonstrated high productivity, creativity, and the ability to identify and successfully tackle important new scientific questions and challenges as demonstrated in their prior research and proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants meeting these criteria may come from any research institutions across the country. Prior productivity and the proposed project's importance are both evidentiary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor expectations for mentored awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Damon Runyon typically looks for mentors who demonstrate their commitment to mentorship through their proposed mentorship plans and have a track record of training scientists who have gone on to have successful scientific careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foundation will fund applications where the mentor is a more recently established independent investigator when a compelling case is made in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection committee composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Damon Runyon award program has a separate selection committee comprised of highly respected, renowned scientists who are the 'phenotype' of the types of researchers that are the focus of the particular award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committees are leaders in their fields and committed to the mission. Chairs and members serve specific terms and rotate off to ensure sustained diversity of expertise and perspectives. Example: Clinical Investigator Award Committee comprises leading translational/clinical researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer feedback policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the Foundation share reviewer feedback with applicants?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No. It is the policy of the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation not to share reviewers’ written comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific application deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Each award program has a specific application deadline (e.g., February 1; March 15; August 15; July 15; July 1; December 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must submit by the listed deadline for the program they are applying to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility based on appointment/title
rubrics_metrics.description: Program-specific eligibility based on appointment/title (examples: Applicants must have initial full faculty appointment; Postdoctoral Fellows; Tenure-track Assistant Professors, Clinical Instructors, Senior Clinical Fellows and Distinguished Fellows; Eligible Damon Runyon Fellows only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must meet the appointment/title criteria for the specific award program they apply to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree type eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Program-specific degree eligibility (examples: MD; MD/PhD; PhD; MD only (cannot be pursuing a PhD)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify degree requirements per award program; some programs restrict degree types or combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award period (duration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Length of the award varies by program (examples: 3 years; 4 years; 2 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award period determines total funding and term commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding per year (budget/levels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual funding amounts differ by program and may be tiered by year (examples: $200,000; Year 1 - $72,000, Year 2 - $74,000, Year 3 - $76,000, Year 4 - $78,000; Year 1 - $100,000, Year 2 - $110,000, Year 3 - $120,000, Year 4 - $130,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should refer to program-specific per-year funding levels and plan budgets accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Total award funding over the award period varies by program (examples: $600,000; $300,000; $100,000; $400,000; $460,000; $240,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total award amount is the cumulative sum of yearly awards; affects project scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other annual funding / benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Program-specific additional benefits (examples: Up to $100,000 of any qualifying medical school debt (over the course of award term); Dependent Child Allowance of $1,000 per child).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some awards include debt assistance or dependent allowances; applicants should check program details for availability and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for continuation or renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a program offers continuation grants or renewal (examples: Yes; 2 additional years; No; No (but Fellows may apply for the Frey Award)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check program rules for continuation eligibility and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentored award status
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the award is a mentored award (Yes/No varies by program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentored awards require a mentor and mentorship plan; non-mentored awards do not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of research funded (basic vs translational)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a program funds translational research, basic research, or both (examples: Translational; Basic or Translational).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure their research type aligns with the program's funded research scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent time devoted to research
rubrics_metrics.description: Program-specific requirement for percent effort devoted to research (examples: 80%; 100% for Level 1 (PhD); 80% for Level 2 (US board certified MD/PhD)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must meet the percent-time commitment specified by the award program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional nomination requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an institutional nomination is required for the program (Yes/No varies by program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 'Yes', applicants must be nominated by their institution per program rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application limits per mentor
rubrics_metrics.description: For each deadline, the number of applications allowed per mentor (examples: 1; N/A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentors may be restricted in the number of mentees they can sponsor per deadline; check program-specific limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application limits per institution
rubrics_metrics.description: For each deadline, the number of applications allowed per institution (examples: 5; N/A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may have caps on the number of applications they can submit for certain programs; applicants should coordinate with institutional officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of reapplications allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of times an applicant may reapply if still otherwise eligible (examples: 1; 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs differ on reapplication limits; applicants should confirm whether previous applicants may submit again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact procedure for awards questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact information for awards-related questions: awards@damonrunyon.org or 212.455.0520.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should use the provided contact info for clarifications about eligibility, deadlines, or program rules.
